clue.text: Songster to banter in church

parts.note: chaff is light teasing talk, a synonym of banter

explanation.surface: A singer is told to keep up the teasing chatter during the church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Songster' reads as a person, but it is a songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: This finch is a common European songbird, and any singing bird can be called a songster.

clue.text: Credit on fish in a basket for it

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so the credit comes first

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: Credit given for fish served in a basket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' points back to the fish in the clue: the answer is the angler's basket for holding fish; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler's wicker basket for carrying the catch is called a creel.

clue.text: Believed to be an antidote for poison found in missile base

definitions.text: Believed to be an antidote for poison

parts.note: an arrow is a missile shot from a bow
a root is the base or foundation of something

explanation.surface: A remedy for poison is said to be found at a rocket launch site.
explanation.walkthrough: The plant's name is said to come from its use by South American peoples to draw poison from arrow wounds; 'found in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This tropical plant's starchy tuber was once thought to counteract poison from arrows.

clue.text: The initial clue — could it dawn on you?

explanation.surface: A question about the first hint: will it suddenly make sense?
explanation.walkthrough: 'dawn on you' means occur to you, but here it means break as day.
explanation.definitionFit: In crosswords a light is an entry, so the first one is the opening clue; the phrase also means daybreak, when day dawns.

clue.text: Candidate with French name in note repeated

parts.note: nom is the French word for name
taken as written

indicators.note: repeated means the note is given twice over

parts.note: E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A candidate with a French name appears in a note twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone put forward for election or office is a candidate, a synonym.

clue.text: Throwing a game

explanation.surface: Throwing a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throwing a game' reads as losing on purpose, but it is two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurling means flinging hard; it is also the Irish stick-and-ball field sport.

clue.text: Allure a flock of goldfinches

explanation.surface: The appeal of a group of small birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Allure is attractive appeal; the collective noun for a group of goldfinches is the same word.

clue.text: The cheek of a fellow!

explanation.surface: Exclaiming at a man's impudence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cheek' reads as impudence, but it is the face.
explanation.definitionFit: Chap is an old word for the jaw or cheek, as in a pig's chap; it is also everyday British for a man.

clue.text: Something worth having when planted

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
set means planted, as seedlings are set out

explanation.surface: A thing of value once it is in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is anything useful or valuable to own.

clue.text: Anger turning up in household or animal enclosure

parts.note: a menage is a household, from the French

indicators.note: turning up suggests the letters are overturned and come out in a new order

parts.note: ire means anger

explanation.surface: Fury erupts in a family home or a zoo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'household' is the French-derived word for a domestic set-up, and 'turning up' rearranges the short word for anger; 'in' and 'or' are links, leaving 'animal enclosure' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A collection of wild animals kept in cages for show, or the place holding them, is a menagerie.

clue.text: Be erratic or blunder

parts.note: to err is to stray from the right course, to be erratic

explanation.surface: A choice between behaving unpredictably and making a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' reads as the link between two definitions, but it supplies its own letters at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A blunder is a mistake, a synonym.

clue.text: Human vice re-stated in Roman list

indicators.note: something re-stated is said again in different form, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A sin is written up afresh in a catalogue kept in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of ROMAN LIST gives the two words; 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In Catholic teaching a deadly sin, one that cuts a person off from grace, is a grave human failing.

clue.text: Game developed from royal contest in court

definitions.text: Game developed from royal contest in court

parts.words: Game developed from royal contest in court
parts.note: the outdoor racket game played on grass grew out of real (royal) tennis, the old indoor game played in an enclosed court

explanation.surface: A sport grew out of a regal match held at the palace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'royal contest in court' sounds like a trial before the monarch, but real tennis, also called royal tennis, is played in a walled court.
explanation.definitionFit: The modern racket sport on grass was devised in the 1870s as an outdoor version of real tennis.

clue.text: Male share speculator

explanation.surface: A man who gambles on stocks.
explanation.definitionFit: A mature male deer; on the stock exchange, someone who applies for new shares hoping to sell them quickly at a profit.

clue.text: Destitute, like a poor boxer

explanation.surface: A penniless man, like a fighter who has been knocked out.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means homeless and penniless; a beaten boxer is knocked down and counted out.

clue.text: Poor mixture to freeze for medicine

indicators.note: a mixture blends things together, so the letters of the word poor are mixed up

parts.note: ice is frozen water; to freeze something is to ice it

explanation.surface: A bad blend chilled to serve as a remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixture' looks like the medicine itself, but it is the anagram signal: POOR mixed up gives OPOR.
explanation.definitionFit: An oporice was an old pharmacy preparation of quinces, pomegranates and other fruit, taken as a remedy.

clue.text: Children tainted source -of water

parts.note: food gone off is spoiled or tainted
a spring is a natural source of water

explanation.surface: Children drink from a polluted well.
explanation.definitionFit: Offspring are a person's progeny: sons and daughters.

clue.text: Bird right for one who grumbles

parts.note: the grouse is a game bird

explanation.surface: A bird is just the thing for a moaner.
explanation.walkthrough: GROUSE is both the bird and a verb meaning to complain, which makes the surface neat.
explanation.definitionFit: To grouse is to complain, so a habitual complainer is a grouser.

clue.text: Cook part upside-down in contrivance allowing water to pass in heating pipe

definitions.text: contrivance allowing water to pass in heating pipe

parts.note: to steam food is a way of cooking it

indicators.note: in a down clue, upside-down means the word part is read from the bottom up

explanation.surface: A chef turns a piece upside down inside a plumbing gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upside-down' turns PART into TRAP; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A device in a steam heating system that lets condensed water out while holding the steam in.

clue.text: Polecat suitable to masticate

parts.note: fit means suitable or appropriate
to masticate is to chew food

explanation.surface: A polecat is well suited to gnawing.
explanation.definitionFit: Fitchew is an old name for the polecat, a small European weasel-like carnivore.

clue.text: Fly going around tree and cleansing

indicators.note: the first word's letters go round the tree's letters, enclosing them

parts.note: to wing is to fly
the ash is a tree

explanation.surface: An insect circles a tree and is washed clean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' looks like the insect, but it is a verb giving WING; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Washing is cleaning with water, so cleansing in action.

clue.text: Free from pretence, seeing that soldiers follow

indicators.note: the soldiers follow, so their letters come after the first piece

parts.note: seeing that means since, because
RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army's corps of military engineers

explanation.surface: Honest, given that the troops come along behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone genuine, with nothing put on, is heartfelt and honest.

clue.text: Operator, well up in progress

parts.note: to well up is to rise or surge, as water or emotion
something going on is in progress

explanation.surface: A machine operator, comfortably off, gets ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well up' reads as prosperous, but it means to rise like water.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon carries out operations, so is one who operates.

clue.text: Spurt in a light shoe

explanation.surface: A sprint in a dancing slipper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: To spurt is to gush out as a liquid driven by a pump does; a plimsoll or dancing slipper is also called by this name.

clue.text: Ample change for a leaf that's symbolic

indicators.note: change tells you to alter the order of the letters of the word ample

explanation.surface: Plenty of alteration for an emblematic leaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The maple leaf is the national emblem of Canada and appears on its flag.

clue.text: Star no more becoming a stargazer

indicators.note: becoming signals that one set of letters turns into another arrangement

explanation.surface: A fading celebrity takes up watching the night sky.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of STAR NO MORE spells the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who studies the heavens scientifically is a stargazer.

clue.text: Perform again and respond to stimulus

explanation.surface: Doing a scene once more and reacting to a cue.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-act is to act a part a second time; to react is to respond to something.

clue.text: Stupid person making an expression of disbelief

explanation.surface: A fool exclaiming that he doesn't believe it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' is a link between the definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A goon is a fool; read as two words it is 'go on!', said when you doubt what you hear.

clue.text: Mischievous child is to ramble around and perform without preparation

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child

indicators.note: to ramble around the word is: the wandering word wraps round it

parts.note: to rove is to ramble or wander
taken as written

explanation.surface: A naughty child wanders about and puts on a show on the spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' makes the wandering verb wrap round 'is'; 'Mischievous child' is a standard crossword source of three letters, and 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To ad-lib is to perform with no rehearsal or script.

clue.text: Botanical sheath from two creatures

indicators.note: from tells you the answer is taken out of the run of letters in the next two words

explanation.surface: A plant casing obtained from a pair of animals.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'twO CREAtures'.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany an ocrea is a tubular sheath formed round a stem by fused stipules, as in docks.

clue.text: Gather information that could be corny?

explanation.surface: Collecting facts that might be trite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corny' usually means trite, but here it means to do with corn, gathered by gleaners in the field.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick up information bit by bit; originally the word meant to gather leftover corn after the harvest.

clue.text: Became ruined — as snooker players may have done

definitions.text: as snooker players may have done

explanation.surface: A business collapsed, as cue sportsmen might have.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for falling into ruin; snooker players aim to sink balls in the pockets, called pots.
